sub_answers.sub_question: What are the dominant experimental systematic uncertainties reported by ATLAS for B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios?
How do uncertainties in B-meson production fractions and fragmentation affect ATLAS branching ratio determinations?
What theoretical inputs (e.g., decay constants, form factors) and their uncertainties enter the interpretation of B→μμ results?
How do differences among experiments or analysis methods create tensions or ambiguities in combined B→μμ constraints?
What model-dependent assumptions (e.g., effective operator basis, lepton-flavor universality) lead to ambiguous theoretical interpretations?
What constraints do the ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− measurements place on the Wilson coefficients in the effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ transitions?
How have ATLAS results influenced global fits of flavor observables addressing lepton-flavor universality or scalar/pseudoscalar couplings?
Which classes of new-physics models (e.g., supersymmetry, Z′, leptoquarks) are constrained by the ATLAS B→μμ branching fraction measurements?
How are ATLAS B→μμ limits incorporated into combined experimental averages (e.g., by HFAG or PDG) used for model exclusion?
What projected improvements in sensitivity would strengthen constraints on flavor-violating couplings from future ATLAS datasets?
What branching ratio for B_s0 → μ+μ− did the ATLAS collaboration report and in which publication/year?
What branching ratio or upper limit for B0 → μ+μ− did ATLAS report and in which dataset or year?
What are the statistical and systematic uncertainties quoted by ATLAS for these branching ratio measurements?
Which datasets (integrated luminosity, collision energy) and triggers did ATLAS use for the rare B→μμ analyses?
What significance or confidence level did ATLAS report for the observation or exclusion of B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− decays?
What muon identification and reconstruction algorithms does ATLAS employ for low-rate B→μμ decays?
What event selection criteria and multivariate classifiers did ATLAS use to separate signal from background in B→μμ searches?
How does ATLAS model and estimate combinatorial and peaking backgrounds in B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− analyses?
What fitting procedures and likelihood functions does ATLAS use to extract yields and branching fractions for B→μμ?
How are detector acceptance, efficiency, and trigger corrections determined and validated in ATLAS B→μμ measurements?

Which experimental systematic error sources (trigger efficiency, muon ID/reconstruction, fit model, background modelling, luminosity, mass scale/resolution) contribute most to ATLAS's reported uncertainties on the B_s0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− branching fraction measurements, and what are their quoted magnitudes?

Quantify how uncertainties in b-hadron production fractions (f_s/f_d, f_u/f_d) and fragmentation functions used by ATLAS propagate into the extracted B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios; which production-fraction inputs are dominant and what alternative fragmentation inputs change the results?

List the theoretical hadronic parameters (e.g., decay constants f_Bs, f_B, bag parameters, short-distance Wilson coefficients, CKM elements) used to convert measured decay rates into branching ratios or NP constraints for B→μμ, and give the stated uncertainties or lattice/perturbative sources that dominate those theory errors.

Compare ATLAS results with CMS, LHCb, and global-fit combinations: what discrepancies arise from different selection strategies, background subtraction, normalisation channels, treatment of peaking backgrounds, statistical methods (profile likelihood vs Bayesian), or input nuisances that produce inconsistent B→μμ constraints?

Identify the analysis-level and theory-level model assumptions (choice of effective Hamiltonian/operator basis, assumptions about lepton-flavour universality, CP-phase conventions, SM branching normalisation, or fixed Wilson coefficients) that, when changed, alter the interpretation of the same B→μμ measurement and introduce ambiguity in new-physics limits.

Which specific combinations of effective-field-theory Wilson coefficients (C9, C10, C9', C10', CS, CP, etc.) are most tightly limited by ATLAS measurements of B_s0 → μ+μ− and what numerical ranges or confidence intervals do ATLAS data alone imply for each coefficient?

In what ways have ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− and related dimuon decay results been used in recent global fits of b→sℓℓ observables (by groups such as EOS, flavio, UTFit or HEPfit) to test lepton-flavor universality or to constrain scalar and pseudoscalar operators; give examples of fit outcomes that change when ATLAS inputs are included or removed.

For concrete new-physics scenarios (e.g., minimal supersymmetric models with large tanβ, Z′ models with flavour non-universal couplings, scalar or vector leptoquark representations), which parameter regions (masses, coupling strengths, tanβ, mixing angles) are excluded or disfavoured by ATLAS measurements of B_s0→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching fractions?

How do ATLAS B_s0→μ+μ− upper limits and measured branching ratios get incorporated into combined experimental averages and likelihoods used by compilers such as the Particle Data Group (PDG), Heavy Flavour Averaging Group (HFLAV/HFAG), or experimental combination papers; what procedures (treatment of correlated systematics, likelihood profiles, use of CLs or Gaussian approximations) are applied to include ATLAS results in model-exclusion studies?

Based on ATLAS upgrade plans and luminosity projections (Run 3, HL-LHC), what are the forecasted precisions or expected upper-limit improvements for B_s0→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− measurements, and how would those projected sensitivities map into tighter bounds on specific flavour-violating couplings or Wilson coefficients (numerical example: reduction in allowed |C_S| or shift in confidence intervals for C10)?

Which value for the branching fraction of B_s0 → μ+μ− did the ATLAS Collaboration publish, and in which specific paper or conference note (title, journal or arXiv identifier) and publication year was it reported?

What branching fraction measurement or 95% (or 90%) confidence-level upper limit for B0 → μ+μ− did ATLAS present, and in which dataset description or year (e.g., Run 1 vs Run 2, integrated luminosity) and publication was this given?

What numerical statistical and systematic uncertainties did ATLAS quote for the measured B_s0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− branching fractions (separately), and how were they reported (absolute error, relative percent, or asymmetric intervals)?

Which ATLAS datasets (specified by center-of-mass energy √s, integrated luminosity in fb−1, and run period) and which trigger selections or muon trigger paths were used in the ATLAS analyses searching for B_s0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− decays?

What significance levels, p-values, or confidence intervals did ATLAS report for the observation, evidence, or exclusion of B_s0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− (e.g., number of standard deviations, CLs upper limits), and where in the publication are these stated?

Which specific muon reconstruction algorithms, track-quality criteria, and identification working points has the ATLAS collaboration applied when reconstructing muons from rare B → μμ decays, particularly in the low-rate regime?

What precise selection cuts, control-region definitions, and machine-learning classifiers (variables, training samples, hyperparameters) has ATLAS implemented to maximize signal-to-background separation in B → μμ analyses?

By what methods does ATLAS quantify and separate combinatorial background from peaking background in B_s0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− searches, including the control samples, mass-sideband techniques, and simulated sources used?

What statistical model forms, unbinned or binned likelihood constructions, background parameterizations, constraint terms, and fitting strategies does ATLAS employ to extract signal yields and convert them into branching-fraction measurements for B → μμ?

How does ATLAS compute detector acceptance, reconstruction and identification efficiencies, and trigger efficiencies for B → μμ channels, and what cross-checks, scale factors from data, and systematic uncertainty evaluations are used to validate those corrections?

Which specific detector- and analysis-related systematic uncertainties does ATLAS list as dominant in its published measurements of the B_s0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− branching fractions (e.g., muon reconstruction/ID, trigger efficiency, mass-resolution, background modelling, normalization-channel yields, integrated luminosity), and what magnitudes are quoted for each?

Quantify how uncertainties in b-hadron production fractions and fragmentation (for example the fs/fd ratio, pT/η-dependent fragmentation functions, and the choice of fragmentation model) propagate into ATLAS’s branching-ratio results — which fractional shift or additional uncertainty do these inputs introduce in the reported B→μμ branching fractions?

List the theoretical inputs used to convert measured event yields into B→μμ branching fractions and limits (for instance decay constants fBs, bag parameters, CKM elements, short-distance Wilson coefficients, ΔΓs/Γs, and NLO/NNLO QCD or electroweak corrections), and give the stated uncertainties or error budgets ATLAS (or the theory papers they cite) assign to each ingredient that affects the numerical interpretation.

What experiment-to-experiment or analysis-to-analysis differences create discrepancies or ambiguity when comparing or combining B→μμ results (for example different normalization channels, treatment of B_s lifetime/ΔΓs, mass-fit models, muon selection, multivariate classifiers, and statistical methods such as profile-likelihood versus Bayesian limits), and where do published comparisons or combination studies identify tensions?

Which explicit model assumptions or theoretical frameworks produce ambiguous or model-dependent interpretations of B→μμ measurements (for example the choice of weak effective operator basis versus SMEFT, assumed lepton-flavour universality, neglect or inclusion of scalar/pseudoscalar and right-handed currents, assumed CP phases, and handling of interference with SM amplitudes), and how do alternative assumptions change the mapping from measured rates to constraints on new-physics parameters?

Which effective operators and specific Wilson coefficients (C7, C9, C10, C_S, C_P and their primed counterparts) are numerically limited by the ATLAS measurement of the B_s^0 → μ^+μ^- branching fraction and lifetime, and what are the updated 95% confidence intervals on those coefficients when ATLAS data alone are used?

In combined phenomenological fits that test lepton-flavor universality and presence of scalar or pseudoscalar interactions, how does inclusion of the latest ATLAS B_s^0 → μ^+μ^- result shift best-fit values and confidence regions for parameters such as C9^μ−C9^e, C10^μ, C_S, and C_P compared with fits excluding ATLAS data?

For explicit classes of beyond-Standard-Model scenarios (R-parity violating and conserving SUSY, heavy neutral gauge bosons Z′ with flavor-changing quark couplings, scalar or vector leptoquarks), what ranges of model parameters (e.g., tanβ and m_A in MSSM, g′/M_Z′, leptoquark Yukawa/coupling × mass) are excluded or tightly constrained by the measured B_s^0→μ^+μ^- branching fraction and effective lifetime reported by ATLAS?

How do ATLAS B_s^0 → μ^+μ^- upper limits and measured central values feed into the world averages and summary tables published by flavor combinations (e.g., HFLAV, PDG, LHCb/ATLAS/CMS combined likelihoods), and what methodology is used to combine ATLAS likelihoods with other experiments when producing exclusion contours for new-physics parameter spaces?

Based on ATLAS upgrade scenarios and projected integrated luminosities (Run 3, HL-LHC 3000 fb^−1), what are the expected improvements in statistical and systematic uncertainty for B_s^0 → μ^+μ^- measurements, and quantitatively how would those improvements tighten projected 95% CL bounds on flavor-violating Wilson coefficients and representative model parameters (e.g., lower limits on M_Z′/g′ or upper limits on leptoquark coupling products)?
What branching ratio for B_s0 → μ+μ− did the ATLAS collaboration report and in which publication/year?
What branching ratio or upper limit for B0 → μ+μ− did ATLAS report and in which dataset or year?
What are the statistical and systematic uncertainties quoted by ATLAS for these branching ratio measurements?
Which datasets (integrated luminosity, collision energy) and triggers did ATLAS use for the rare B→μμ analyses?
What significance or confidence level did ATLAS report for the observation or exclusion of B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− decays?

Which specific muon reconstruction and identification algorithms does ATLAS apply when reconstructing low-rate B→μ+μ− decays (e.g., combined muons, standalone MS, segment-tagged, inside-out ID), including any low-pT or boosted-B specialized tweaks, software releases or algorithm versions used, and the selection thresholds/quality flags applied in published B→μμ analyses?

What were the exact event preselection and final-selection criteria plus any multivariate classifiers used by ATLAS to separate B→μ+μ− signal from background: list kinematic and topological cuts (pT, η, vertex χ2, flight-length significance, IP/impact-parameter requirements), isolation or vertexing variables, the type of classifier (BDT/NN), the input variables to that classifier, training/validation samples, and the working-point/score cut values reported in the analysis notes or papers?

How did ATLAS construct and validate the models for combinatorial and peaking backgrounds in Bs0 and B0 → μ+μ− searches: specify the functional forms or templates used for sideband combinatorial background, the identified peaking sources (e.g., B→h+h− with hadron→μ misID, B→hh′, charmonium feed-down), the methods for obtaining shapes (MC vs data-driven templates), how hadron-to-muon misidentification rates were measured and applied, and which control channels or sidebands were used to constrain each background component?

What fitting framework and likelihood strategy did ATLAS employ to extract signal yields and convert them to branching fractions for B→μ+μ−: state whether unbinned/ binned extended maximum-likelihood fits were used, the parametric PDFs chosen for signal (Crystal Ball, Gaussian, double-Gaussian, MC-derived kernel), background PDFs, simultaneous category fits or simultaneous mass-and-discriminant fits, treatment of nuisance parameters and systematics (profile likelihood, constraints), and the statistical procedure for limits or significance (CLs, profile-likelihood ratio, asymptotic/ toy MC)?

How are detector acceptance, reconstruction and trigger efficiencies determined and validated for ATLAS B→μ+μ− measurements: describe the MC samples and generator/settings used for acceptance, the derivation of per-muon and per-event reconstruction and trigger scale factors from data (tag-and-probe on J/ψ→μ+μ−, Z→μμ), kinematic/η/pileup reweighting procedures, closure tests with control channels such as B+→J/ψK+, and how systematic uncertainties on these corrections were estimated and propagated into the branching-fraction measurement?
